title: fix(sdk): preserve declared MIME for base64 image responses
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16351

- Preserves `media_type` when resolving base64 image items, allowing SVG responses to produce correct image metadata and data URLs.
- Retains PNG fallback, URL-response MIME handling, response bytes and array order for generation and editing.
- Adds image-resolution regressions and controls: three fail before the fix; all ten focused tests and 117 SDK tests pass afterward.
- Verification: strict typecheck, ESM/CJS/browser/declaration builds, Biome, independent focused tests, and built-SDK native loopback checks pass. No live provider calls or Pollen used.

gist.headline: SVGs keep their name tags
gist.blurb: An SVG should arrive as an SVG, even when it travels as base64. The SDK keeps its MIME label attached, so image metadata and data URLs describe the pixels correctly.
gist.summary: The SDK preserves `media_type` when resolving base64 image items, producing correct SVG metadata and data URLs while retaining the PNG fallback, URL-response MIME handling, response bytes, and image order in generation and editing.
gist.impact: Developers receiving base64 SVG images get the declared MIME type in their metadata and data URLs; PNG fallbacks and other image-response behavior stay intact.
gist.visual_concept: Depict an SDK image response as a little SVG picture carrying a clearly marked MIME tag through a retro computer, with a PNG picture nearby to represent the fallback. Polli helps the CRT monitor robot read the tag; code-plants make the scene feel like a small, well-tended workshop.
